# UX Checklist: Persistent Dark Mode Icon

**Purpose**: Review whether the dark mode feature requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable for user-facing behavior and layout expectations.
**Created**: 2026-08-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the required public page types fully enumerated so "all public site pages" is not left open to interpretation? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec define whether any non-public, error, or system pages are intentionally excluded from dark mode icon coverage? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the expected visual states of the icon control documented, including how readers distinguish light-mode and dark-mode actions? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for both desktop and mobile navigation contexts where the top-right area may already contain other controls? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "top-right area of the viewport" precise enough to produce one consistent placement across pages and breakpoints? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "floating control" defined clearly enough to distinguish viewport-pinned behavior from header-attached or page-flow behavior? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "modern" intentionally translated into objective UI requirements, or is it still an implicit design interpretation left outside the spec? [Ambiguity, Spec §Input]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "visible while scrolling" clarified for pages with sticky headers, overlays, or very short content where scrolling behavior differs? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §FR-003]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do the placement requirements remain consistent between the clarification answer, user stories, and functional requirements? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §User Story 1, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK010 Do the overlap-avoidance requirements align with the requirement that the icon remain persistently visible on all pages? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK011 Are persistence expectations consistent between the user stories, functional requirements, and success criteria for cross-page theme retention? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-006, Spec §SC-004]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 Can "consistent floating top-right viewport location" be objectively reviewed without an explicit tolerance or placement rule? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "100% of tested long pages" measurable without defining which pages count as the required long-page test set? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "one interaction" sufficiently specific about keyboard, touch, and pointer activation expectations? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK015 Do the success criteria define how reviewers should judge whether the icon blocks important content or navigation? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for readers arriving with a previously saved theme preference before any new interaction occurs? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements complete for switching theme from every major page class named in the spec, not just the home page and long articles used in examples? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK018 Are alternate interaction scenarios addressed for keyboard-only and assistive-technology users beyond the generic need to activate the icon? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec define what should happen if the icon cannot safely occupy the top-right area because of competing UI in a specific layout? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are zero-scroll or near-zero-scroll page scenarios fully specified so the icon remains discoverable without causing layout crowding? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Are very long mobile reading scenarios specified with enough detail to judge when the floating icon becomes obstructive? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for theme-control behavior during page transitions or initial page load when the saved theme and rendered theme may briefly differ? [Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK023 Are accessibility requirements explicitly specified for labeling, focus indication, and target usability, rather than implied by the control's presence? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK024 Are performance expectations for immediate theme switching and lack of disruptive layout shift stated in the spec, not only in planning artifacts? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 Are responsive layout expectations specific enough to judge whether the control remains usable across common mobile and desktop breakpoints? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]

## Dependencies And Assumptions

- [ ] CHK026 Is the assumption that the existing theme system remains valid documented strongly enough to prevent hidden redesign scope from leaking into implementation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK027 Are dependencies on current navigation structure or existing theme preference behavior identified clearly enough for reviewers to assess impact? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities And Conflicts

- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec define what "important reading or navigation content" includes so overlap judgments are not subjective? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK029 Is there any unresolved ambiguity between "show in all pages" from the original request and "all public site pages" in the formal requirements? [Ambiguity, Spec §Input, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK030 Is an explicit requirement ID and traceability scheme sufficient for reviewers to map every scenario and success criterion back to a functional requirement? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
